CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  August 27, 2024

The City of Signal Hill appreciates your attendance. Citizen interest provides the Council and
Agency with valuable information regarding issues of the community. Meetings are held on
the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of every month.

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view the meeting live at 7:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  • Charter Spectrum Channel 74 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
To participate (closed session at 6:00 p.m. and regular meeting at 7:00 p.m.):

  • In-person Participation: Council Chamber of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, August 27, 2024.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.

(12)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

  a.  CIVIC CENTER MASTER PLAN ADOPTION

  Summary:

  Last year, the City began working on the Civic Center Master Plan (CCMP). The
  purpose of the CCMP is to work with our community to reimagine the Civic
  Center and incorporate desired amenities that will serve future residents. In
  December 2023, the City Council selected “The Campus” as the desired
  alternative which emphasizes the construction of a new amphitheater, active
  and passive recreational elements, and a new Community Center. Given the
  large scope and related cost associated with developing the project, the CCMP
  is divided into three primary phases. Phase 1 of the CCMP, which includes the
  amphitheater and expanded parking lot along 21st street, is in the
  pre-development phase. Phases 2 and 3 include a new community center,
  sports courts, playground, improvements to Jessie Nelson Circle, and
  accessibility improvements. The purpose of this discussion is to provide the City
  Council with an opportunity to provide additional feedback regarding the final
  Civic Center Master Plan as well as the proposed funding and phasing plan. As
  the project continues developing, staff will return to update the City Council
  regarding progress on various elements including final design, bidding,
  construction, and funding opportunities.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning  Government:  Strengthen  internal
  communication, recruitment, retention systems, and processes to
  increase the effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. Adopt the Civic Center Master Plan substantially in the form presented.

  2. Discuss the proposed Phasing and Funding Plan associated with the Civic
  Center Master Plan and provide staff with additional direction as desired.
  b.  ACCEPTANCE OF GREENLATINOS URBAN & COMMUNITY FORESTRY
  PROGRAM SUBAWARD GRANT AGREEMENT FOR THE STREET TREE
  PLANTING - FEDERAL PROJECT

  Summary:

  Page 3 of 13
 City Council  Regular  August 27, 2024

  The City Council adopted the 2023 Street Tree Master Plan (STMP) with the
  goal of to restoring and expanding the City’s urban forest canopy. Following the
  City’s adoption of the STMP, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest
  Service made competitive grants available to plant and maintain trees to
  enhance and expand the nation’s urban forestry. On September 14, 2023, the
  USDA approved the City as a sub awardee, granting $1,000,000 in funding for
  its Street Tree Planting - Federal Project (Project). GreenLatinos, a national
  pass-through partner for the USDA Forest Service, will collaborate with the City
  throughout the duration of the Project to ensure implementation of and
  compliance with the terms of the grant agreement. The City Council will consider
  acceptance of grant funds for the Project and authorize the City Manager and /or
  Public Works Director to execute the grant agreement and all necessary
  documents to receive and expend awarded grant funds.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1: Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience

  Goal No. 4: Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, ACCEPTING GRANT FUNDS FROM GREENLATINOS FOR
  THE STREET TREE PLANTING - FEDERAL PROJECT

  2. Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND AUTHORIZING
  BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 FOR STREET
  TREE PLANTING - FEDERAL PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,000,000

  3. Authorize the City Manager and/or Public Works Director to administer the
  grant agreement and all necessary documents to receive and expend
  awarded grant funds.
  c.  PLANNING COMMISSION VACANCY

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider opening a recruitment to fill an unscheduled
  vacancy on the Planning Commission to serve the remainder of the vacant term
  through May 31, 2025.

  Page 4 of 13
 City Council  Regular  August 27, 2024

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):
  Goal No. 5  High Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.

  Recommendations:

  1. Declare the vacancy of one Planning Commissioner position.

  2. Authorize staff to open a recruitment seeking residents interested in serving
  as a Planning Commissioner for the remainder of the vacant term through
  May 31, 2025. The recruitment will run from August 30 through September

(13)  CONSENT CALENDAR

  a.  WAIVE THE READING OF ORDINANCES IN FULL AND AUTHORIZE
  READING BY TITLE ONLY

  Summary:

  The recommended action waives reading of ordinances in full and authorizes

  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Government Code Section 87300 et. seq., requires local governments to review

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING RESOLUTION NO. 2023-07-6758, AMENDING THE
  CONFLICT OF INTEREST CODE FOR THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  d.  APPROVE TRANSFER AGREEMENT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT - SAFE, CLEAN WATER PROGRAM FOR
  Page 6 of 13
 City Council  Regular  August 27, 2024

  MUNICIPAL PROGRAM AND RESOLUTION APPROVING A LIST OF
  PROJECTS TO BE FUNDED BY THE PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25

  Summary:

  On November 6, 2018, Los Angeles County voters approved Measure W, a
  parcel tax aimed to address regional water capture water and reduce reliance on
  imported water. Measure W imposes a tax of 2.5 cents per square foot of
  impermeable surface area on private property in the Los Angeles County Flood
  Control District (District), generating approximately $285 million annually for the
  countywide Safe, Clean Water (SCW) Program. For the City to receive its share
  of collected funds, the City must enter into the Los Angeles County Transfer
  Agreement and submit an Annual Plan. The City Council will also consider
  adopting a resolution to incorporate a list of projects and programs to be funded
  by the SCW Measure W for Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Endure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Waive further reading and adopt the following resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL.
  CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A TRANSFER AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT AND THE CITY OF
  SIGNAL HILL, AGREEMENT NO. 2024MP75 FOR THE SAFE, CLEAN WATER
  PROGRAM - MUNICIPAL PROGRAM

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Transfer Agreement between the
  City and the Los Angeles County Flood Control District, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney.

  3. Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, APPROVING THE LIST OF PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 TO BE FUNDED BY SAFE, CLEAN WATER
  PROGRAM - MEASURE W FUNDS

  4. Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND AUTHORIZING
  Page 7 of 13
 City Council  Regular  August 27, 2024

  BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25
  e.  CONTINUANCE OF THE PROCLAMATION OF THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY IN RESPONSE TO FEBRUARY 2024 WINTER STORMS AND
  REAFFIRMING EMERGENCY CONDITIONS REQUIRING EMERGENCY
  ACTION TO COMPLETE EMERGENCY REPAIRS AT PANORAMA
  PROMENADE AND MOLINO AVENUE AND 20TH STREET

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider authorizing the City Manager to extend the
  proclamation of the existence of a local emergency in response to the February
  2024 winter storms for 60 days. At the February 27, 2024, meeting, the City
  Council authorized the City Manager to extend the proclamation of the existence
  of a local emergency. The City Council adopted a Resolution, by a four-fifths
  vote, declaring authority to the City Manager or his designee, pursuant to Public
  Contract Code Sections 20168 and 22050, to enter into an emergency public
  works contract. The City Council also approved a Public Works contract with
  Zimprich Engineering Incorporated, for a not-to-exceed amount of four hundred
  thirty-one thousand nine hundred ten dollars ($431,910), for emergency work
  pertaining to the Panorama Promenade Trail and the Molino Avenue and 20th
  Street slope immediate repair projects.

  The City Council subsequently adopted resolutions, by a four-fifths vote,
  authorizing the City Manager, or his designee, pursuant to Public Contract Code
  Section 22050, to continue emergency storm damage repairs at the Panorama
  Promenade Trail and Molino Avenue and 20th Street. The City Council will
  consider adopting a Resolution authorizing the City Manager, or his designee,
  pursuant to Public Contract Code Section 22050, to continue emergency storm
  damage repairs at the Panorama Promenade Trail and Molino Avenue and 20th
  Street. Staff requests the City Council authorize the City Manager to extend
  proclamation of the existence of a local emergency in response to the February
  2024 winter storms for 60 days. Staff recommends the City Council, by a
  four-fifths vote, reaffirm the emergency continues to exist and, therefore, the
  emergency contract work must continue to be done without a public bidding
  process.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  Page 8 of 13
 City Council  Regular  August 27, 2024

  1. Authorize the City Manager to extend the proclamation of the existence of a
  local emergency in response to the February 2024 winter storms for 60 days.

  2. Adopt a resolution, by four-fifths vote, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, DECLARING THE NEED TO CONTINUE THE EMERGENCY
  CONTRACTING AUTHORITY DELEGATED TO THE CITY MANAGER, OR HIS
  DESIGNEE(S), PURSUANT TO PUBLIC CONTRACT CODE SECTION 22050
  f.  PROPOSED ACCEPTANCE OF THE EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT
  PERFORMANCE (EMPG) 23 GRANT AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION
  APPROVING BUDGET AMENDMENT

  Summary:

  The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) implements grant
  programs that support the DHS/Federal Emergency Management Agency
  (FEMA). The focus of these grants is to enhance resiliency and preparedness
  for emergencies. The City has been awarded the Emergency Management
  Performance Grant (EMPG) 23 funding in the amount of $40,000. The grant
  funding would be used to offset City costs to update the City’s Emergency
  Operations Plan, develop a Crisis Communications Plan, and fund training costs
  for the Emergency Management Coordinator. Staff recommends the City
  Council authorize the City Manager to accept the grant and adopt a resolution
  authorizing a budget adjustment to increase grant revenue by $40,000 and
  related expenditures.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to accept grant funding through the Emergency
  Management Performance Grant (EMPG) 23 grant.

  2. Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL
  HILL, CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND
  AUTHORIZING BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2024-25
  g.  RESOLUTION ACCEPTING AN EASEMENT FOR THE PURPOSES OF

  Page 9 of 13
 City Council  Regular  August 27, 2024

  CONSTRUCTING AND MAINTAINING A BLOCK WALL ACROSS A PORTION
  OF PROPERTY LOCATED AT 2398 CALIFORNIA AVENUE

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider approving a resolution accepting a public

  portion of private property located on Assessor’s Parcel Number 7211-021-001.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintaining community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendation:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, ACCEPTING CERTAIN EASEMENT TO THE CITY OF SIGNAL
  HILL FOR THE PURPOSES OF CONSTRUCTING AND MAINTAINING A
  BLOCK WALL ACROSS CERTAIN REAL PROPERTY AT ASSESSOR
  PARCEL 7211-021-001
  h.  MASTER  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  WITH  GENTRY  GENERAL
  ENGINEERING INCORPORATED FOR STREET AND ALLEY MAINTENANCE
  AND IMMEDIATE REPAIR SERVICES

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider entering into a Master Services Agreement with
  Gentry General Engineering Incorporated for the Citywide Alley Improvement
  Project and as-needed immediate repair services. Under the proposed
  agreement, Gentry General Engineering would perform the scope of work in the
  Citywide Alley Improvement Project and serve on an as-needed basis to provide
  immediate repair services at sidewalks, streets, and alleys throughout the City. If
  approved by the City Council, the proposed agreement would serve for a term of
  one year, at a not to exceed amount of $450,000.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendation:

  Page 10 of 13
 City Council  Regular  August 27, 2024

  Authorize the City Manager to award a Master Services Agreement to Gentry
  General Engineering Incorporated for as-needed street, alley, and immediate
  repair services for a term of one year, for a not-to-exceed amount of $450,000 in
  a form approved by the City Attorney. The term of this proposed agreement is
  for one year with the option of no more than three additional one-year
  extensions.
  i.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT REGISTER DATED AUGUST 27, 2024

  Summary:

  The Contract Amendment Register is a listing of proposed contract amendments
  and project change orders eligible for streamlined processing based upon the
  following criteria as documented in the City’s Purchasing Policy:

  ·  The City Council authorized funds with the adopted fiscal year Operating
  Budget;
  ·  Staff are satisfied with the goods/services received to date; and
  ·  The City Manager reviewed and approved each amendment for
  streamlined processing.

  Staff is presenting one contract amendment for City Council consideration as
  follows:

  1) Michael Baker International, Inc. (MBI): This consultant provides support for
  various Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Permanent Local
  Housing Allocation (PLHA) programs. The proposed amendment would
  formalize a contract 180-day discretionary term extension (Attachment B.2)
  which was agreed upon by the City and MBI and approved as to form by the
  City Attorney on June 27, 2024. The proposed Second Amendment would
  extend the term for an additional six months through June 30, 2025, and
  increase the contract not-to-exceed contract amount to $110,000.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No.1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize the Contract Amendment Register dated August 27, 2024.
  j.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS AND MONTHLY TRANSACTION REPORT

  Summary:

  The Schedule of Investments is a listing of all surplus funds invested for both the

  k.  WARRANT REGISTER DATED AUGUST 27, 2024

  Summary:

CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday
  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.
